headline: A1-B4 was hit hardest, 0.04201 vs 0.03588 for the flipped A1-B3 (17.1% more), and the closed-form prediction closely tracked the ranking (Spearman 0.980).
idea: False-negative labels at one hospital shift the shared model, so the error spreads to other hospitals' subgroups.
A closed-form propagation vector predicts each recipient subgroup's damage without retraining.
Damage depends on how far a subgroup's mean projects onto that vector, and the most-affected subgroup can be a different one entirely.
findings: The closed-form prediction closely matched the retrained effects: Spearman 0.980 [0.974, 0.986] and slope c 1.002 [0.982, 1.023], against the paper's 0.975 [0.961, 0.987] and c = 1.014 for A1-B3. Flipping 30% of A1-B3 positives changed 45.5 labels per seed (0.379%), close to the paper's 45.25 (0.377%).

A1-B4 was hit hardest, with a mean logit decrease of 0.04201 [0.03405, 0.04630], against the paper's 0.04225, and 17.1% more than target-matched A1-B3 (0.03588). The paper reports 18.2% and rank 2 for A1-B3, and this run gives rank 2 as well. The audit gives 5 of 8 source errors a different top victim, with 8 of 64 predicted cells negative (the recipient's logit rises).

try_next.why: The audit predicts A1-B1 as its own top victim, unlike A1-B3, so this tests whether same-group damage dominates.

try_next.why: Splits recipients by client and tests the paper's heterogeneous setting, where it reports Spearman 0.974 for A1-B3.

try_next.label: No association between A and R
try_next.why: With r_shift 0, A0 and A1 recipients should look more alike along the propagation vector.

caveats: Synthetic data from the paper's setup; logistic regression only, with Newton's method replacing FedAvg rounds (same optimum).
A lower logit does not necessarily flip a prediction; Spearman over eight averaged group effects is a coarse measure.
